$comment: Practice scripts (draft for academic-team review) — single source for the browser mock and the FastAPI backend. kind: programme (the 15-day course, by week) | anytime (rehearse on demand) | baseline (first friendly chat). minLevel: 1 calm · 2 surprise follow-up · 3 worried · 4 upset or fast-talking. knownFixes.pattern is a case-insensitive regex. Bump "version" to push script changes into existing databases.

moments.title: Morning Greeting at Drop-off
moments.scene: Ria’s mother at the gate, in Ria’s first week of school.

turns.parentLine: Good morning, Priya ma’am! Ria is a little nervous today.

hint.text: Good morning! Don’t worry, she will settle in quickly. We will start with her favourite songs.

turns.demoReply: Good morning. Don’t worry, she settle quickly.

turns.parentLine: Ma’am, please give her this cough syrup at eleven. Five ml.

hint.text: Sure. Just to confirm: five ml of the cough syrup at eleven o’clock?

turns.demoReply: Okay ma’am, I give her syrup at eleven.

knownFixes.better: Sure. Just to confirm: five ml of the cough syrup at eleven o’clock?

turns.parentLine: She cried a lot last night about school.

hint.text: That is normal in the first week. Many children feel this way, and it gets better every day.

turns.demoReply: That is normal in the first week. Many children feel this way, and it gets better every day.

turns.parentLine: Oh, and I forgot — she is allergic to peanuts.

hint.text: Thank you for telling me. Just to confirm: no peanuts at all. I will tell the nanny too.

turns.demoReply: Thank you. No peanuts, I will tell to nanny.

knownFixes.better: Thank you for telling me. No peanuts at all. I will tell the nanny too.

turns.parentLine: Can I stay with her for ten minutes?

hint.text: Yes, you can stay for a few minutes. Then a short, happy goodbye works best.

turns.demoReply: Yes, you can stay. Then short goodbye is best.

knownFixes.better: A short, happy goodbye works best.

turns.parentLine: Her uncle will pick her up today, not me.

hint.text: Thank you. Is he on the pickup list? Please tell me his name, and I will check his ID.

turns.demoReply: Okay. He is in the pickup list? Tell me his name please.

knownFixes.better: Is he on the pickup list? Please tell me his name.

turns.parentLine: What if she asks for me during the day?

hint.text: We will comfort her and keep her busy. I will call you if she needs you.

turns.demoReply: We will comfort her and keep her busy. I will call you if she needs you.

turns.parentLine: Last week another child pushed her. Will someone watch her properly?

hint.text: I understand your worry. We watch the children closely, and I will keep her near me today.

turns.demoReply: I understand. We are watching all children closely.

turns.parentLine: Ma’am, I’m late for work, I can’t stay — just tell me, will she be fine or not?

hint.text: Yes, she will be fine. Please go, and I will message you if she needs anything.

turns.demoReply: Yes she will be fine, you go, I message you.

knownFixes.better: Yes, she will be fine. Please go, and I will message you if she needs anything.

turns.parentLine: Thank you, ma’am. What time should I pick her up?

hint.text: Please come at twelve thirty. I will tell you how her day went.

turns.demoReply: Please come at twelve thirty. I will tell you how her day went.

lesson.title: Drop-off: calm and clear
lesson.intro: Parents share important details at the gate. Say them back so nothing is missed.

phrases.text: Just to confirm: five ml at eleven?
Is he on the pickup list?
Thank you for telling me. No peanuts at all.
Don’t worry, she will settle in quickly.

lesson.tip: Use “will” for promises about later: “I will call you”, not “I call you”.

moments.title: Pick-up Update
moments.scene: Kabir’s father at pick-up time, asking how the day went.

turns.parentLine: Hello ma’am! How was Kabir today?

hint.text: Hello! Kabir had a lovely day. He was happy and joined in everything.

turns.demoReply: Hello! Kabir have a lovely day. He was happy and joined in everything.

turns.parentLine: Did he eat his lunch?

hint.text: Yes, he finished most of his lunch. He did not like the carrots.

turns.demoReply: Yes, he finished most of his lunch. He do not like the carrots.

knownFixes.better: He did not like the carrots.

turns.parentLine: What did the class do today?
turns.demoReply: We painted leaves and we read a story about a little seed.

turns.parentLine: Was he playing with other children?

hint.text: Yes, he played with Meera and Dev in the sand pit.

turns.demoReply: Yes, he played with Meera and Dev in the sand pit.

turns.parentLine: Why is there a little mark on his arm?

hint.text: He bumped his arm on the slide. We put a cold pack on it, and he was fine after a few minutes.

turns.demoReply: He bump his arm on slide but he is fine.

knownFixes.better: He bumped his arm on the slide, but he was fine after a few minutes.

turns.parentLine: He says someone took his crayons.

hint.text: Thank you for telling me. I will check, and we will practise sharing tomorrow.

turns.demoReply: Thank you for telling me. I will check and we practise sharing tomorrow.

knownFixes.better: I will check, and we will practise sharing tomorrow.

turns.parentLine: Does he need anything for tomorrow?

hint.text: Please send a water bottle and a spare set of clothes.

turns.demoReply: Please send a water bottle and spare clothes.

turns.parentLine: He has been very quiet at home. Is something wrong at school?

hint.text: Thank you for telling me. He seems happy here, but I will watch him closely and tell you what I see.

turns.demoReply: He is happy here only. I will watch him.

turns.parentLine: Someone took his crayons again! This is the second time this week!

hint.text: I am sorry. I understand this is upsetting. I will speak to the children today and update you tomorrow.

turns.demoReply: Sorry. I will talk to children and tell you tomorrow.

turns.parentLine: Is there any homework?
turns.demoReply: There is no homework, but you can ask him about the seed story.

turns.parentLine: Thank you so much. See you tomorrow!

hint.text: You are welcome. See you tomorrow, Kabir!

turns.demoReply: You are welcome. See you tomorrow, Kabir!

lesson.title: Pick-up: a two-line summary
lesson.intro: Start with one good thing about the day, then one useful detail.

phrases.text: He had a lovely day. He enjoyed painting.
He bumped his arm, but he was fine after a few minutes.
Please send a water bottle tomorrow.

lesson.tip: Talk about today in the past tense: “He played”, “She ate”, “They painted”.

moments.title: Parent Meeting
moments.scene: A meeting with Anaya’s mother about her progress.

turns.parentLine: Good afternoon. Thank you for meeting me.

hint.text: Good afternoon! Thank you for coming. Please have a seat.

turns.demoReply: Good afternoon! Thank you for coming. Please have a seat.

turns.parentLine: How is Anaya settling in this term?

hint.text: She has settled in well. She is confident and makes friends easily.

turns.demoReply: She has settled in well. She is confident and makes friends easily.

turns.parentLine: Does she listen during circle time?

options: Sometimes she finds it hard to…

turns.demoReply: Most days she listens well. Sometimes she finds it hard to wait for her turn.

turns.parentLine: Is she talking more in English now?

hint.text: Yes, she uses full sentences now, especially during play.

turns.demoReply: Yes, she use full sentences now, especially during play.

knownFixes.better: Yes, she uses full sentences now, especially during play.

turns.parentLine: Why do they only play? When will they start proper studies?

hint.text: Children learn best through play. When they build with blocks, they learn numbers, shapes and teamwork.

turns.demoReply: They learn by playing only. Blocks teach numbers.

turns.parentLine: What about numbers? Can she do maths?
turns.demoReply: She can count to twenty and she is good at sorting shapes.

turns.parentLine: Her writing looks very messy to me.

hint.text: That is normal at this age. Her grip is getting stronger every week.

turns.demoReply: That is normal at this age. Her grip is getting stronger every week.

turns.parentLine: How can I help her at home?
turns.demoReply: You could read a short story every night and try asking her to retell it.

turns.parentLine: She doesn’t want to share her toys with her brother.

hint.text: We are practising turn-taking in class. A sand timer can help at home too.

turns.demoReply: We are practising turn-taking in class. A sand timer can help at home too.

turns.parentLine: Is there anything I should worry about?

hint.text: No, she is doing well. We will keep working on patience and listening.

turns.demoReply: No, she is doing well. We will keep working on patience and listening.

turns.parentLine: Other children already read books. Is she falling behind?

hint.text: Every child learns at her own pace. Anaya is doing well, and here is one thing you can try at home.

turns.demoReply: Every child is different. She is doing good.

knownFixes.better: Every child learns at her own pace. Anaya is doing well.

turns.parentLine: Honestly, I’m not happy. We pay so much and I see no progress!

hint.text: I understand. Let me show you her work from June and from now. Then we can plan the next steps together.

turns.demoReply: I understand. I will show you her June work and now work.

turns.parentLine: When can we talk again?
turns.demoReply: We can meet again next month, and you can message me any time.

turns.parentLine: Thank you, this was really helpful.

hint.text: Thank you for your support. Anaya is a joy to teach.

turns.demoReply: Thank you for your support. Anaya is a joy to teach.

lesson.title: Parent meetings: strengths first
lesson.intro: Open warmly, share a strength, then one thing to work on and one activity for home.

phrases.text: She is confident and makes friends easily.
Children learn best through play.
One thing you can try at home is reading together.
Thank you for coming. Please have a seat.

lesson.tip: For a child, use “she is / he has”: “She is kind.” “He has many friends.”

moments.title: Worried or Upset Parent
moments.scene: Arjun’s mother is upset because he came home with a scraped knee.

turns.parentLine: Arjun came home with a hurt knee and nobody told me!

hint.text: I am really sorry. You should have heard it from us. Let me explain what happened.

turns.demoReply: I am really sorry. You should have heard it from us. Let me explain what happened.

turns.parentLine: What happened exactly?

hint.text: He tripped while running in the playground. We cleaned the scrape and put a plaster on it.

turns.demoReply: He tripped while running in the playground. We cleaned the scrape and put a plaster on it.

turns.parentLine: Why wasn’t anyone watching him?
turns.demoReply: Two teachers were outside. It happened very quickly, but we helped him at once.

turns.parentLine: I don’t want this to happen again.

hint.text: I understand. We will remind the children to walk near the steps.

turns.demoReply: I understand. We will remind the children to walk near the steps.

turns.parentLine: Can you give him extra attention from now on?

hint.text: I can’t promise extra attention for one child, but I will keep a close eye on him and update you.

turns.demoReply: I cannot give extra attention but I will see him.

turns.parentLine: I want to complain. Who is responsible for this?

hint.text: I understand. I will ask our centre head to meet you today, and I will be there too.

turns.demoReply: I will tell to centre head to meet you.

knownFixes.better: I understand. I will ask our centre head to meet you today.

turns.parentLine: This is not acceptable! I’m thinking of taking him out of this school!

hint.text: I am sorry you feel this way. Please give us a chance to fix this. Can we meet with the centre head tomorrow?

turns.demoReply: Sorry you feel like this. Give us one chance please.

turns.parentLine: Will you call me next time?

hint.text: Yes, I will call you straight away if anything happens.

turns.demoReply: Yes, I will call you straight away if anything happens.

turns.parentLine: Okay. Thank you for listening.

hint.text: Thank you for telling me. Arjun is safe with us.

turns.demoReply: Thank you for telling me. Arjun is safe with us.

lesson.title: Worried parents: acknowledge, explain, next step
lesson.intro: First show you understand, then give the facts, then say what happens next.

phrases.text: I understand why you are worried.
Let me explain what happened.
Here is what we will do next.
I can’t promise that, but I can update you every day.
Let me ask our centre head to join us.

lesson.tip: Say sorry for the feeling, then the facts: “I am sorry this upset you. He tripped while running.”

moments.title: Admission Enquiry Tour
moments.scene: Mr. Mehta is visiting the school before applying for his daughter.

turns.parentLine: Hello, I would like to know about admissions for my daughter.

hint.text: Welcome! I am happy to show you around. How old is your daughter?

turns.demoReply: Welcome! I am happy to show you around. How old is your daughter?

turns.parentLine: She is three and a half. What will she learn here?
turns.demoReply: Children learn through play. Every day we sing, read and explore outside.

turns.parentLine: How many children are in a class?

hint.text: There are twenty children in each class, with two teachers.

turns.demoReply: There are twenty children in each class, with two teachers.

turns.parentLine: Is the school safe?

hint.text: Yes. We have CCTV, a guard at the gate, and only known adults can pick children up.

turns.demoReply: Yes. We have CCTV, a guard at the gate, and only known adults can pick children up.

turns.parentLine: How do you keep parents updated?
turns.demoReply: We share photos every week and you will get a report every term.

turns.parentLine: Thank you. What is the next step?

hint.text: Please fill in the form at the front desk. We will call you to book a visit day.

turns.demoReply: Please fill in the form at the front desk. We will call you to book a visit day.

lesson.title: Welcome a new family
lesson.intro: Be warm, answer simply, and ask a question back.

phrases.text: Welcome! I am happy to show you around.
Children learn through play, songs and stories.
There are twenty children in each class, with two teachers.

lesson.tip: Ask a question back to keep it friendly: “How old is your daughter?”

moments.title: A Parent Calls
moments.scene: Dev’s mother calls the school early in the morning.

lesson.title: Phone calls: slow and clear
lesson.intro: On the phone there is no face to help. Speak slowly and repeat names and times.

phrases.text: Good morning, this is Dev’s teacher. How can I help you?
Thank you for letting me know.
Please send his name and photo before tomorrow.

lesson.tip: Repeat times to check: “Tomorrow at twelve thirty, yes?”

turns.parentLine: Hello, is this Dev’s class teacher?

hint.text: Yes, good morning. This is Dev’s teacher. How can I help you?

turns.demoReply: Yes, I am Dev teacher. Tell me.

knownFixes.better: Yes, good morning. This is Dev’s teacher. How can I help you?

turns.parentLine: Dev has a fever, so he won’t come today.

hint.text: Oh, I am sorry to hear that. Thank you for letting me know. I hope he feels better soon.

turns.demoReply: Oh sorry. Thank you for telling. Get well soon.

turns.parentLine: Can you send me today’s activities?

hint.text: Yes, I will send you today’s activities on the class group this evening.

turns.demoReply: Yes, I will send in evening on group.

turns.parentLine: Also, can his grandfather pick him up tomorrow?

hint.text: Yes, but he must be on the pickup list. Please send his name and photo before tomorrow.

turns.demoReply: Yes but he should be in pickup list.

knownFixes.better: Yes, but he must be on the pickup list. Please send his name and photo.

turns.parentLine: Okay, thank you so much.

hint.text: You are welcome. Take care, and please tell Dev we miss him.

turns.demoReply: Welcome. Take care. We miss Dev.

moments.title: A Small Incident
moments.scene: Meera’s father at pick-up. Meera slipped while playing and has a small bump.

lesson.title: Small incidents, calmly
lesson.intro: Facts first, then how the child is now, then the next step.

phrases.text: She slipped while playing. We put a cold pack on it right away.
She was playing happily again after a minute.
Please watch her tonight.

lesson.tip: Use the past tense for what happened: “She slipped”, “We cleaned it”.

turns.parentLine: What is this bump on Meera’s head?

hint.text: She slipped while playing and bumped her head. We put a cold pack on it right away.

turns.demoReply: She slip while playing. We put ice.

knownFixes.better: She slipped while playing and bumped her head.

turns.parentLine: Did she cry a lot?

hint.text: She cried for a minute, and then she was playing happily again.

turns.demoReply: She cried one minute, then she played.

turns.parentLine: Should I take her to the doctor?

hint.text: She was fine all day, but please watch her tonight. If she feels sick or very sleepy, please see a doctor.

turns.demoReply: She is fine, but watch her tonight.

turns.parentLine: Why didn’t you call me?

hint.text: It was a small bump and she was fine, so we planned to tell you at pick-up. Next time I will call you.

turns.demoReply: It was small, so we did not call.

turns.parentLine: Okay, thank you for telling me.

hint.text: Thank you for understanding. I will check on her first thing tomorrow.

turns.demoReply: Thank you. I will check her tomorrow.

moments.title: Celebration Day
moments.scene: Kiara’s mother asks about the Diwali celebration at school.

lesson.title: Events: clear times and plans
lesson.intro: Give the time, what to bring, and what parents can do.

phrases.text: It starts at ten. Please drop her by nine forty-five.
Parents are welcome to watch.
She can wear traditional clothes.

lesson.tip: “By nine forty-five” means not later than nine forty-five.

turns.parentLine: Ma’am, what should Kiara wear for the Diwali celebration?

hint.text: She can wear traditional clothes. Please avoid anything too long, so she can move easily.

turns.demoReply: She can wear traditional dress.

turns.parentLine: What time does the programme start?

hint.text: It starts at ten. Please drop her by nine forty-five.

turns.demoReply: It is starting at ten.

turns.parentLine: Can parents come and watch?

hint.text: Yes, parents are welcome. Seats are in the hall, and the show lasts about an hour.

turns.demoReply: Yes, parents can come. It is one hour.

turns.parentLine: Do we need to send any sweets?

hint.text: No need, thank you. We are serving healthy snacks to all the children.

turns.demoReply: No need. We give snacks.

turns.parentLine: Okay, see you on Friday!

hint.text: See you on Friday. Kiara will love it!

turns.demoReply: See you Friday.

moments.title: Say Hello to ELSA
moments.scene: A friendly first chat. Nothing is scored — ELSA just gets to know you.

turns.parentLine: Hi! I’m ELSA. It’s lovely to meet you. Tell me a little about your class.
turns.demoReply: I teach Pre-K. My class has eighteen children.

turns.parentLine: What do you enjoy most about being a teacher?
turns.demoReply: I enjoy when children learn new words.

turns.parentLine: Think of a parent you spoke to this week. What did you talk about?
turns.demoReply: A parent asked me about lunch.
